slides.title: 3HAG: 3 Year Highly Achievable Goal
slides.headline: 3HAG: 3 Year Highly Achievable Goal
notes: The 3HAG connects long-term ambition to annual and quarterly execution.
The method builds confidence in predicting growth and making it happen.
slides.support: A 3-year stepping stone toward the BHAG.
body: Connect the future company to the capabilities and targets needed to get there.

artwork.alt: The cascade from BHAG to priorities: BHAG, 3HAG, 1HAG, QHAG, then individual quarterly priorities. Each level is built from the one above it and directs the one below. 3HAG is highlighted: this is where we are.

slides.title: Your 3HAG on one page.
slides.headline: Your 3HAG on one page.

artwork.alt: Example 3HAG page for the same subscription business as the KFFM example. Year 3 ends December 31, 2029. 1, Numbers, each with an owner. Gross revenue $12 million, Andrew. Profit margin 20%, Allison. Cash in the bank $3 million, Allison. Widgets: 20,000 subscription leads and 8,000 marketing qualified subscription leads, Chris. 2,000 new subscriptions, Andrew. 1,900 activated subscriptions, Jen. 48,000 collected payments, Allison. Profit per subscription $600 a year, Allison. Head count 70, Pat. 2, Statement: the subscription service our customers can’t imagine running without. 3, Key capabilities. Marketing that brings in qualified leads. A sales team that adds new MRR every month. Activation in a day, without hand-holding. Billing that collects on time, every time. 4, Known for: up and running in a day.

hotspots.tip: One sentence that describes the company you will become in 3 years. No numbers.
The 3 to 5 things that must be in place to make the numbers and the statement true.
What people should think when they hear your company name, 3 years from now.

Jim Collins’s economic engine, from Good to Great. It is the one profit ratio that, raised steadily over time, does the most to drive your economics. Here, profit per subscription: profit divided by the average number of active subscriptions. Allison owns hitting the target.

notes: This is what we will build together today: one page, four blocks. By the end of the day this page is yours.
Same subscription business as the KFFM example. The five widgets are the five hand-offs on that map, counted for Year 3.
Every number has an owner, the same owner it will have in the 1HAG and QHAG. In Metronome each 3-year target sits on a metric, and every metric has an owner.
The numbers hang together. About 4,000 subscribers at roughly $250 a month is $12 million. And 4,000 subscribers paying monthly is 48,000 collected payments.
The statement has no numbers. Each capability strengthens one function on the map. Known for is what customers would say.

slides.title: What are your 3-year targets?
slides.headline: What are your 3-year targets?
notes: Introduce 3HAG as the 3-year Highly Achievable Goal. Have each leader write targets independently, then share and agree. Record exact units and the future date. Distinguish cash from profit.
Agree on gross revenue, ending cash and widgets, using consistent definitions across all three horizons. The 3HAG fiscal measures are gross revenue and cash.

body: Gross revenue, margin and year-end cash, for Year 3 alone.
Name the widget for each hand-off on your KFFM. Estimate the quantity where you can.
Name an owner for every number.

slides.title: What will the company be in 3 years?
slides.headline: What will the company be in 3 years?
notes: Each leader writes a statement, then the team agrees. The statement and financial targets must describe the same future. Follow the source instruction to keep numbers out of the statement.
slides.support: Write one sentence that describes the company you will become.

artwork.alt: The 3HAG page with block 2, the statement, highlighted.

hotspots.tip: One sentence that describes the company you will become in 3 years. No numbers.

slides.title: What 3 to 5 capabilities must be in place?
slides.headline: What 3 to 5 capabilities must be in place?
notes: Ask each leader to propose capabilities, group overlaps and agree on 3 to 5. These are Kick Off capabilities, not fully validated differentiators. Ask what the company must become able to do. Use the same capabilities when selecting annual priorities.
A capability is something the company becomes able to do. A market rank or financial target is an outcome.
Test each proposed capability against the targets and statement before agreeing on it.

artwork.alt: The 3HAG page with block 3, key capabilities, highlighted.

hotspots.tip: The 3 to 5 things that must be in place to make the numbers and the statement true.

slides.support: What must be in place to make the numbers and the statement true?
body: If revenue tripled, what would we need to be able to do?

slides.title: What do you want to be known for?
slides.headline: What do you want to be known for?
notes: Collect individual answers, then agree. Check consistency with the statement and capabilities. Do not replace this prompt with a brand-promise workshop.
slides.support: In 3 years, when someone says your company name, what should people think?

artwork.alt: The 3HAG page with block 4, known for, highlighted.

hotspots.tip: What people should think when they hear your company name, 3 years from now.

slides.title: Does your 3HAG pass?
slides.headline: Does your 3HAG pass?
notes: Ask a leader to read the plan aloud. Invite the team to identify contradictions and untested assumptions.
Check the team captured each field. Record unresolved assumptions for validation without reopening every agreed phrase.
Do the widget volumes, conversion rates and prices support the revenue target? Which assumption explains any gap? Anything that fails goes on the homework list with an owner.
At a quarterly, test it against what the Market Map showed. Change only what fails or is no longer true.

artwork.alt: The planning cascade with the 3HAG checked; the 1HAG, QHAG and individual priorities are still to come.

slides.support: Read it aloud before you move on.
body: The numbers are set: date, revenue, cash and widgets.
The statement and known for describe the future company.

slides.title: 3 years means 12 quarters of progress.
slides.headline: 3 years means 12 quarters of progress.
notes: The 3-year direction becomes annual plans and quarterly commitments.
The team reviews and learns each quarter instead of writing a plan once and leaving it untouched.

artwork.alt: A continuous line of 12 loops climbing from Today to the 3HAG. Each loop is one quarter, Q1 to Q12, grouped into Year 1, Year 2 and Year 3. Q4 and Q8 are each a 1HAG; Q12 lands the 3HAG. The line fades from blue to green. Each loop: plan the quarter, do the work, review and learn.
